topology: single Linux host; isolated two-node Redis primary/replica containers; manually promoted replica; not Sentinel/Cluster; application verifier in Node runner

acknowledgement_semantics.primary_only: SET NX returns OK; no replica confirmation
acknowledgement_semantics.wait: SET then WAIT 1 1500 on same Redis connection; check actual replica count
acknowledgement_semantics.wait_insufficient: replica detached; WAIT 1 250 returns actual count, fail closed unless >=1
acknowledgement_semantics.waitaof: AOF enabled with appendfsync always on both nodes; SET then WAITAOF 1 1 2000 on same connection; check local and replica counts

fault: docker SIGKILL primary after recorded acknowledgement; manually promote the only replica with REPLICAOF NO ONE; replay identical proof to promoted replica
limitations: no Sentinel or Redis Cluster automatic failover
no real network partition; replication is administratively detached for primary-only/insufficient-ack cases
no MySQL or three resource-service processes

persistence_by_condition.waitaof_local_replica_acked: AOF on; appendfsync always on primary and replica; RDB off

fault_procedure.primary_only_detached: Synchronize replica; disconnect replica from isolated Docker network; close replica-to-master session; verify role=replica and master_link_status=down; SET NX gets primary reply; SIGKILL primary; reconnect replica; manually promote; replay same proof.
fault_procedure.wait_replica_acked: Synchronize replica; SET NX then WAIT 1 1500 on same connection; require actual count >=1; SIGKILL primary; manually promote; replay.
fault_procedure.wait_ack_insufficient: Disconnect replica and close replication session; SET NX then WAIT 1 250 returns zero; fail closed; SIGKILL; reconnect and promote replica; replay same proof.
fault_procedure.waitaof_local_replica_acked: AOF+appendfsync always on both nodes; SET NX then WAITAOF 1 1 2000 on same connection; require local=1 and replica=1; SIGKILL primary; manually promote; replay.
